crime.value: Murder by strangulation-style killing, the body concealed in a hermetically sealed deed box at a solicitors' firm; a second murder (Miss Chittering) follows to silence a witness. Central question: who put the body in the sealed box, and when — dating the death and breaking alibis
crime.quote: a dead body is found at the firm's premises at Lincoln's Inn, concealed within a hermetically sealed deed box

victim.value: Marcus Smallbone, a small grey elderly trustee of the Ichabod Stokes Trust — killable because as co-trustee he could uncover Abel Horniman's fraudulent mortgage/embezzlement; second victim Miss Chittering, a typist who knew of the green rucksack purchase
victim.quote: After she'd killed Smallbone… The killing of Miss Chittering and the efforts to throw the blame on to Bob.

closed_world.value: The offices of Horniman, Birley and Craine, solicitors, in Lincoln's Inn — a small, routine-bound firm of partners, clerks and secretaries with access to the deed boxes; deserted on a Saturday morning
closed_world.quote: the firm's premises at Lincoln's Inn… Lincoln's Inn is a very deserted place on Saturday morning

culprit_and_motive.value: Miss Cornel, Abel Horniman's long-serving devoted secretary, killed Smallbone (the deep motive never fully known, apparently to protect Abel's memory and conceal his irregular mortgage fraud), then killed Miss Chittering in self-defence to avoid exposure, framing Bob Horniman
culprit_and_motive.quote: "If Miss Cornel was mad," he was saying, "then I'm mad, and you're mad."

resolution.value: Bohun traces the chain from the disposal of the trust papers in a green rucksack left at London Bridge Left Luggage Office; the rucksack was sold by Miss Chittering's fiancé who recognised Miss Cornel — she is arrested and pleads guilty, escaping hanging
resolution.quote: this particular rucksack should have been sold to her by the head of the Camping Department of Messrs. Merryweather and Matlock

investigator.value: Dual lens: Henry Bohun, newly qualified solicitor in the firm and gifted amateur detective (insider-suspect), working alongside Chief Inspector Hazlerigg's official police investigation
investigator.quote: Henry Bohun's sleuthing is an even more significant component of the book than Hazlerigg's official investigation.

suspect_architecture.value: Partners and staff of the London law firm Horniman, Birley and Craine: senior partners Birley and Craine, junior partner Bob Horniman (son of the late Abel Horniman, whose fraudulent mortgage supplies motive), solicitor John Cove, secretaries Miss Cornel (the eventual killer, secretary of twenty years devoted to Abel), Miss Chittering (later a victim), Miss Bellbas, Anne Mildmay, plus clerks Prince, Waugh, Hoffman and Sergeant Cockerill. Amateur detective Henry Bohun and Chief Inspector Hazlerigg investigate from inside the firm.
suspect_architecture.quote: Several of those present will shortly become suspects in a murder case when a dead body is found at the firm’s premises

red_herring.value: Multiple cultivated false trails: suspicion deliberately thrown onto Bob Horniman by the murderer, the romantic entanglements (Anne Mildmay/John Cove/Bob Horniman), Eric Duxford's secretive private business, and the bizarre-but-coincidental fact that the body's box held papers of the trust of which the victim was trustee.
red_herring.quote: as full of cunningly-suggested red herrings

clue_fairness.value: Clues are staged openly for the reader in the finest Golden Age tradition, including two floor plans; the crucial green rucksack clue is spoken aloud in the secretaries' room in front of the whole staff and Bohun before its significance is understood.
clue_fairness.quote: two floor plans are supplied in the finest Golden Age tradition

social_world.value: The hierarchical world of a Lincoln's Inn solicitors' firm in austerity post-war Britain: partners lord it over clerks and secretaries, Birley bullies subordinates dependent on their jobs, Craine paternalistically harasses female staff, and the founder Abel Horniman's 'Horniman system' and reputation govern everything, including the concealment of his fraudulent mortgage.
social_world.quote: Since Mr. Prince stood in considerable awe of Mr. Birley, and in even greater fear of losing his job, he was a very convenient whipping-block.

alibi.value: Alibis turn on office movements and timing — Bohun compiling a list of who came in on which day — with a post-war electricity cut playing a notable part in establishing alibis; the murder was timed for a Saturday morning when Miss Cornel knew she would be alone in the office.
alibi.quote: with an electricity cut playing a notable part in the establishing of alibis

reveal_mechanic.value: A single thread of physical causation: the green rucksack used to remove the trust papers, deposited at London Bridge Left Luggage Office, was sold to Miss Cornel by the head of the Camping Department who was Miss Chittering's fiancé; his recognition, and Miss Chittering's public mention of 'her big green rucksack', links her to the crime and explains the second murder. Corroborated by evidence of rolling screws and left wrists; she finally pleads guilty.
reveal_mechanic.quote: The single thin, unbreakable thread of causation which joined the body of Marcus Smallbone to the Left Luggage Office

media_and_audience.value: The firm's public reputation is the governing audience: the partners suppress details of Abel Horniman's irregular mortgage, smooth down clients' susceptibilities, and Craine funds Miss Cornel's defence — the scandal managed institutionally rather than publicly narrated.
media_and_audience.quote: dealt firmly with their scruples about suppressing the details of Abel’s most irregular mortgage

investigator_wound.value: Bohun is an insider investigating his own colleagues, which forces him to trade on friendship — he deliberately perpetrates 'thundering indiscretions' and dockets confidences he never invited for future use, privately calling himself and others liars.
investigator_wound.quote: He hadn’t invited the confidence, and he felt no scruple in docketing it for future reference.

victims_enemies.value: Marcus Smallbone was co-trustee of the Ichabod Stokes trust and thus the one man positioned to uncover Abel Horniman's fraudulent mortgage — making him a threat to Abel's reputation and to Miss Cornel, Abel's fiercely loyal secretary of twenty years. The firm's partners and staff (Birley, Craine, Bob Horniman, John Cove) all had friction with the trust and with each other.
victims_enemies.quote: dealt firmly with their scruples about suppressing the details of Abel's most irregular mortgage

suspect_wounds.value: Bob Horniman is vulnerable through his inherited partnership resting on an almost complete lack of technical knowledge and his concealed romantic possessiveness over Anne Mildmay; Anne Mildmay is visibly 'off colour' and hiding distress; John Cove conceals a rejected courtship, a drunken night in Bow Street cells, and shady dealings with a grey little 'Mr. Brown'; Eric Duxford has private business conducted on office time.
suspect_wounds.quote: On Bob's face... Bohun saw a look which he had no difficulty in recognising. Half of it was made up of possession and the other half of apprehension.

unreliable_frame.value: Almost every account within the firm is partial or self-serving: the secretaries cannot agree who entered on what day, Bob Horniman lies about not caring, John Cove performs flippancy over real feeling, and Miss Cornel's calm, helpful testimony is the deepest deception of all. Bohun himself withholds and manipulates information to provoke reactions.
unreliable_frame.quote: "Liar," said Henry. But this was to himself, after Bob had left the room.

setting_as_constraint.value: The Lincoln's Inn law office of Horniman, Birley and Craine, governed by Abel Horniman's rigid filing 'system': any misplaced bundle of papers would be noticed within twenty-four hours, forcing the murderer to remove the Stokes papers from the building entirely. Lincoln's Inn is deserted on a Saturday morning; the hermetically sealed, air-tight deed boxes permit concealment for weeks; post-war electricity cuts shape the alibis.
setting_as_constraint.quote: In this office they would have been noticed in twenty-four hours—the fat would have been in the fire with a vengeance.

evidence_type.value: Testimonial/physical convergence: the retail identification of a purchased object — a large green rucksack sold by the head of the Camping Department at Merryweather and Matlock, who recognised Miss Cornel and described the rucksack to his fiancée Miss Chittering — plus the Left Luggage Office deposit at London Bridge holding the excised trust papers. Supporting physical evidence: rolling screws and the murderer's left-handedness.
evidence_type.quote: this particular rucksack should have been sold to her by the head of the Camping Department of Messrs. Merryweather and Matlock

false_suspect.value: Bob Horniman, onto whom Miss Cornel deliberately tried to throw the blame after the second killing; also broadly the partners and clerks framed by circumstance, with Anne Mildmay and John Cove drawing suspicion through concealed personal entanglements.
false_suspect.quote: The killing of Miss Chittering and the efforts to throw the blame on to Bob.

technical_detail.value: Solicitors' office practice: the air-tight, hermetically sealed deed box as a body-concealing container; the ability to steal or copy a box key and select the box least likely to be opened; knowledge that unclaimed Left Luggage parcels are opened after six months; and the excision by nail scissors of every reference to the firm from account books and schedules of investments to render papers unidentifiable. Also the fraudulent 'puisne' mortgage in trust accounting.
technical_detail.quote: One of the boxes, so handy, so capacious, so fortunately air-tight. She selects the one least likely to be opened

moral_ambiguity.value: Miss Cornel killed not from greed but out of a twenty-year devotion to Abel Horniman, protecting the memory of a man she alone saw the better side of — a swindler of corporations who nonetheless never touched the pennies entrusted to him for poor old ladies. Her subsequent killing of Miss Chittering was, as Bohun frames it, self-defence: a woman fighting for her life. Craine and Bohun refuse to call her mad or monstrous.
moral_ambiguity.quote: "If Miss Cornel was mad," he was saying, "then I'm mad, and you're mad. We're all of us mad."
